searchText: <@607055410104500244> and I were working on a simple builder implementation and noticed that the `prev_randao` value is kind of hard to come by unless you've already been sent a `forkchoiceUpdate` by some beacon node. I've proposed a new beacon API endpoint here that would make it a bit easier to get access to this value: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/242 Would other people building MEV-tools find this useful? cc <@539495253418180618> The approach that works best for our open builder (https://github.com/flashbots/boost-geth-builder) is to have a modified beacon-node that triggers the block building process with a payload that contains all the information needed: https://github.com/flashbots/prysm/blob/develop-boost/beacon-chain/blockchain/execution_engine.go#L257 Btw, in addition to our Goerli relay, we've opened block submissions to external builders on our Sepolia MEV-Boost relay: https://boost.flashbots.net/mev-boost-status-updates/flashbots-sepolia-relay-now-accepts-external-block-submissions (our mainnet relay also allows external builder submissions) I think the solution to this is a low-cost "cancellation" transaction and/or low-cost "expired" transactions. If a transaction exists with an expiration, the expired transaction can be included but it would only validate the signature and update the nonce. This should bring the operational cost *below* 21,000 gas, so the cost of an expired transaction landing on-chain would be quite low to the user while still protecting the system from DoS attacks. Makes sense. I would like to upstream something like this in Lighthouse eventually so that builders don’t need their own fork. The flashbots-lighthouse diff is quite small so I think we could just put something equivalent behind a `--always-prepare-payloads` flag Similarly, if there was a special transaction type that *only* bumped the nonce, it should cost less than 21,000 gas and thus allow for "cheap" cancellations. I don't see how that would bring cost below 21k gas, or why it would be cheaper than a regular ETH transfer. You still need to include a tx (=storage), broadcast it (=bandwidth), and validate the signature (=EC operation) no? Hmm.. Nice thought An ETH transfer requires looking up two accounts, updating the balance of both, updating the nonce of one of them, and validating the signature. A cancellation transaction only requires looking up one account, updating its nonce (not balance), and validating the signature. It is strictly cheaper (operationally). The big difference is one vs two cold account lookups. I don't know *how much* cheaper, but we can assert that it is strictly less than a transfer. well, a cancellation transaction should also pay for the costs of the signature validation of the tx it is cancelling right? That is defended against with the 12.5% replace-by-fee increment requirement most clients implement. Ah yes, so.. depending on gas costs, it might still be more expensive overall (if gas costs are not at least 12.5% less) And already accounted for with the transfer transaction gas costs (so still strictly less). Yeah, if you are cancelling a 21,000 gas transaction with a 20,900 gas transaction it actually costs more in fees to be included vs not. This is why I think there is separately value in expiring transactions (which also are healthier for the network as they keep the mempool/network clear of additional cancellation transactions. It does feel like it opens up new ways of DDoSing nodes, but that gut feeling might be wrong though The key is to ensure that anyone who sends something to the network *must* pay (eventually) for that. This is why expiring transactions can't just become invalid. They can, however, change their behavior to something less costly. i certainly would the approach i have been taking is to essentially MiTM the FCU call to grab the payload attributes but would strongly support client changes so that e.g. we don't need to run forks of clients to have efficient builders fwiw, i think fcU is too late, you can start building way before on newPayload already all attributes are known https://github.com/flashbots/prysm/blob/develop-boost/beacon-chain/blockchain/execution_engine.go#L257 and yes, certainly agree for standard support! an SSE subscription would fit best into the current model i think would love a SSE subscription to newPayload events, with BuilderPayloadAttributes as data (slot, blockHash and prevRandao is needed)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I think the solution to this is a low-cost "cancellation" transaction and/or low-cost "expired" transactions.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If a transaction exists with an expiration, the expired transaction can be included but it would only validate the signature and update the nonce.  This should bring the operational cost *below* 21,000 gas, so the cost of an expired transaction landing on-chain would be quite low to the user while still protecting the system from DoS attacks.

excerpts.content: Makes sense. I would like to upstream something like this in Lighthouse eventually so that builders don’t need their own fork. The flashbots-lighthouse diff is quite small so I think we could just put something equivalent behind a `--always-prepare-payloads` flag

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
